claims.text: Increasing Al or Ti content in a CoCrFeMnNi-based HEA coating can push the alloy toward a phase-stability limit and create a metastable microstructure.
A metastable HEA microstructure can undergo a stress-induced phase transformation during mechanical deformation.
The proposed stress-induced phase transformation will occur during wear of an HEA coating.
The deformation-induced transformation produces a harder or stronger secondary phase.
Formation of the transformed phase reduces the coating's wear rate.
The baseline CoCrFeMnNi-based coating is near a phase-stability limit but is not sufficiently tuned to transform appreciably during wear.
A slight increase in Al or Ti relative to the baseline promotes metastability and transformation susceptibility.
The relevant structural mediator is the emergence of a secondary phase in the near-surface wear region.
The transformed phase accommodates strain and increases work hardening.
Transformation-mediated strain accommodation mitigates extensive material removal during abrasive wear.
The Al/Ti-modified coating will have a lower wear rate than the baseline under identical wear conditions.
The Al/Ti-modified coating will show clearer near-surface phase-transformation signatures than the baseline.
A minimum applied stress or load is required to activate the transformation.
The mechanism should operate at room temperature between the transformation threshold and the onset of catastrophic failure.
Alternative failure mechanisms at extreme loads can dominate and suppress the proposed TRIP-mediated wear benefit.
In situ X-ray diffraction and post-test electron microscopy can be used to detect the proposed near-surface phase transformation.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says the transformation localizes plastic deformation, while also presenting strain accommodation and mitigation of extensive removal as beneficial. The cited mechanistic evidence instead says transformation-induced hardening slowed strain localization, so the stated role of localization is internally unclear.
